roles.description: RBAC roles scoped to this organization. Assign permissions per role; users get the union of permissions across all roles they hold.

platformPerms.title: Platform permissions
platformPerms.description: The global permission keys available for assignment to any role.

create.title: New role
create.description: Create a custom role for this organization. Assign permissions afterwards.

permsSheet.title: Permissions — {{name}}
permsSheet.description: Toggle to grant or revoke. Changes apply immediately to every user holding this role.
permsSheet.grantAction: Grant this permission to the role
permsSheet.revokeAction: Revoke this permission from the role

available.title: Available permissions
available.description: Permissions you can add to this role. Granting takes effect immediately.
available.empty: Every permission is already granted to this role.

permissions.description: The complete catalogue of permission keys you can grant to roles. These are global to the platform; bindings to roles live under each organization.

policies.description: Organization-wide security policy. Applies to every login, every session, every API call against this organization.

network.title: Network access
network.movedToRules: Which networks may sign in is set by IP rules, which every sign-in to this organization is checked against.

password.title: Password policy
password.description: Enforced at signup, password change, and password reset.

session.title: Session policy
session.description: Affects new sessions only; existing sessions keep their original lifetime.
session.maxAgeHelp: How long a session lasts after sign-in, however active it is. Also how long an application stays signed in. A duration such as 24h, 720h (30 days) or 2160h (90 days); between 1h and 8760h.
session.idleHelp: A session ends once it goes this long without being used. At least 15m and no longer than the maximum session age, such as 30m, 8h or 24h.
session.limitEvict: End their least recently used session
session.limitHelp: How many places one person may be signed in at once. A session ended this way can't be renewed; anything it already holds stops working within 10 minutes.

mfa.title: MFA enforcement
mfa.description: Who must use a second factor to sign in. Anyone who must and has none sets up an authenticator app before they get in.
mfa.optional: Optional — only people who set up a second factor are asked for it
mfa.required: Required — everyone uses a second factor to sign in
mfa.adminOnly: Admins only — anyone whose role can change anything (a write permission)
mfa.noteHelp: Applies to password sign-in. People an administrator marks as requiring MFA must use it whatever this is set to.
mfa.graceHelp: For this many days after you turn the requirement on, people who already have an account can skip setting up a second factor; they're asked each time they sign in. 0 means no grace period.

stepUp.title: Step-up for sensitive actions
stepUp.description: Before someone changes factors, keys, secrets, sign-in settings or other sensitive things, they confirm a second factor again. A confirmation counts only in the browser where it was made.
stepUp.windowHelp: How long a confirmation keeps sensitive actions unlocked in that browser. Signing out, a password change or a factor reset ends it sooner.
stepUp.methodsHelp: Only these confirm a sensitive action. People who hold none of them aren't asked to confirm changes to their own factors.

validation.maxSessions: Use a number from 1 to 1,000, or leave it empty for no limit.
validation.duration: Enter a duration, such as 24h or 30m.

relationships.description: Zanzibar-style relationship tuples: object #relation subject. Write relationships, browse them, and expand the identity graph.

write.title: Write relationship
write.subjectHelp: A user, or a userset such as group:eng#member, which expands recursively.
write.description: For example object document:readme, relation viewer, subject user:… or group:eng#member.

check.title: Check relationship
check.description: Resolve whether a user has a relation to an object; the decision is kept in the Decision Explorer.

tuples.title: Browse tuples
tuples.description: List every relationship stored on an object.
tuples.deleteDescription: {{tuple}} is removed, and any access it granted ends at once.

graph.title: Identity graph
graph.description: Expand every subject reachable from an object and relation, with cycle-safe traversal.
graph.empty: No relationships found from this object+relation.

validation.object: Enter an object, such as document:readme.
validation.relation: Enter a relation, such as viewer.
validation.subject: Enter a subject.

resources.description: The protected resources RBAC permissions are scoped to. Derived from the permission catalogue — each resource exposes a set of actions you can grant to roles.

catalogue.title: Resource catalogue
catalogue.description: One row per resource, with the actions it exposes.
catalogue.empty: No permissions registered, so no resources to show.

check.title: Access Tester
check.description: Evaluate a permission for a specific user and see exactly why access is granted or denied — including which role granted it and whether it came directly or through a group.
check.runDescription: Permissions use the resource:action shape, e.g. users:read.
check.userIdHelp: The UUID of the user to evaluate.
check.resultDescription: The decision and the grant-path trace the authorization engine walked.
check.resultPlaceholder: Run a check to see the allow/deny decision and how it was reached.
check.deniedReason: No role grants this permission to this person in this organization.
check.grantPathsHint: Each path is an independent reason the permission is held.
check.noGrantPath: Allowed, but no explicit grant path was returned.

validation.userId: Enter the person's user ID (a UUID).

groupRoles.title: Roles
groupRoles.description: Members of this group inherit these roles’ permissions.
groupRoles.emptyTitle: No roles granted to this group yet.
groupRoles.emptyDescription: Use the selector above to grant a role — every member inherits its permissions.
groupRoles.revokeTitle: Remove this role from the group?
groupRoles.revokeDescriptionPlain: Members will lose the permissions granted by {{name}} unless they hold it through another group or a direct assignment.
groupRoles.grantAction: Grant this role to the group
groupRoles.revokeAction: Remove this role from the group

overview.description: A single view of your authorization posture: what's configured, what's risky, and what changed.

health.title: Policy health
health.subtitle: Overall configuration health and risk summary.

bandHint.fair: A few findings are worth reviewing.

coverage.title: Resources protected
coverage.subtitle: Resources with authorization policies.
coverage.ringLabel: {{percent}}% of resource types covered by a policy
coverage.caption: Resources protected

changes.title: Recent policy changes
changes.subtitle: From the audit log
changes.empty: No authorization changes in this window.

unconditional.title: Unconditional allow policies
unconditional.description: Enabled allow policies with no condition match everything.

disabled.title: Disabled policies
disabled.description: Policies that exist but are not enforced.

build.title: Start building
build.subtitle: Quick actions to manage your authorization setup.

analytics.title: Evaluation analytics
analytics.subtitle: Allow-vs-deny trends, latency, and decision volume from the authorization engine.
analytics.unavailableTitle: Decision metrics aren't being collected yet
analytics.unavailableBody: Allow-vs-deny volume, p95 decision latency and policy-evaluation counts will appear here once the authorization engine emits decision metrics. Everything above is read from live configuration and the audit log.

abac.deleteDescription: “{{name}}” stops applying to access decisions at once. This can’t be undone.

editor.description: Define the effect, target and condition.
editor.name: Name

test.title: Test against the live engine
test.description: Evaluates a request against every enabled policy and explains the decision.

simulator.description: Ask a what-if question of any engine and see the exact allow or deny decision, explained.

request.title: Request
request.description: Fill in the subject, resource and action to evaluate.

decision.title: Decision
decision.empty: Run a simulation to see the decision.

batch.title: Batch simulation
batch.description: Evaluate one resource and action for up to {{cap}} subjects, against the live decision point.
batch.subject: Subject
